text:
maya: FYI — Platform changed quota deduction semantics in canary this morning: we now charge on response completion instead of request start. Noticed our e2e SDK tests started failing with quota errors. anyone on-call for SDKs?

raj: saw that too. my integration against dedicated infra jumped quota at end-of-stream and then we got OOM-ish retries. console per-route numbers didn't line up with tenant totals.

emily: quick summary from platform side: goal was to avoid double-charging aborted streams. We moved deduction from pre-request to post-response to reflect actual tokens rendered. We missed that some client libs (esp older Go/TS) call the API with an expectation that the quota header is authoritative at request time.

david: @emily can you share the checklist you used for the rollout? was there a migration header?

emily: rollout notes: 
- canary in us-west-2 
- opt-in header `X-Quota-Mode: post` 
- default switched after 2h to reduce false positives 
I thought the header shim would cover older SDKs but apparently some SDKs ignore unknown headers.

lee: in Go SDK we parse `X-Quota-Estimate` and pre-decrement a local token bucket to avoid client-side spamming. that assumption breaks with post-charge. we can make the parser conservative but need a coordinated plan.

sarah: console UX note: per-route dashboard shows "tokens_requested" while tenant overview shows "tokens_charged" — we should label them and add an annotation for the switch. saw PM escalate.

maya: action items I propose: 
1) roll back default to `pre` until SDK patch lands OR enable `X-Quota-Mode` opt-in only 
2) SDKs add safe-fallback when quota headers missing/unknown 
3) Console add a migration annotation and reconciliation job for the 4h window
4) Telemetry: add event `quota.mode.changed` so we can slice by client version

raj: +1. Also: add a short-lived server-side compatibility header `X-Quota-Legacy` with values `pre`/`post` so SDKs can explicitly switch. That avoids version-dependent heuristics.

emily: we can add `X-Quota-Legacy` flag. Concern: rollout complexity increases. but feasible.

david: SDK side notes: Python/TS have easier rollouts; Go releases are slower because of downstream consumers. we should publish a compatibility shim in the Go client that preserves pre-decrement behavior behind a flag. suggestion: `client.Config{QuotaMode: "legacy"}` and also honor header if present.

lee: sample patch for Go shim (pseudo):
```go
// if server sets X-Quota-Legacy: pre => maintain old decrement
if hdr := resp.Header.Get("X-Quota-Legacy"); hdr == "pre" {
    client.localBucket.Decrement(estimate)
}
```
We'll open a PR today.

sarah: console: we'll add an annotation and a line-item in the quota dashboard that shows both "estimated" and "charged" during migration window. UX copy: "We changed quota accounting; please reconcile client versions."

emily: telemetry: I'll add `quota.mode.changed` and include fields: mode, server_ts, rollout_id, client_accept_header. That'll help debug.

maya: timeline proposal: rollback default to `pre` now, enable opt-in `post` with `X-Quota-Mode: post` for canary customers, land SDK patches within 48h, enable `X-Quota-Legacy` for 72h for alignment, then re-evaluate.

raj: +1. also communicate to SRE and support with a short blurb and sample remediation steps.

deploy-bot: deploy status: rollback to `pre` default initiated by @emily — canary rollback in progress (job 8421). ETA ~9m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: thanks. once PRs are up, tag me and I'll coordinate release notes and a small console banner.

lee: opening Go PR now — will link when ready.

emily: thanks all. I'll post the rollout checklist and the header contract in #eng-platform once rollback completes.

maya: quick follow-up: could we add a small test in our sdk-integration-suite that simulates partial stream aborts and asserts final quota balances? that would've caught this.

david: good idea. I'll add a flaky-tolerant test harness in the next run.

maya: ok closing loop for now. keep thread updated with PR links and console ticket. :thumbsup:
